html:
SMTO-LLM-0029 — The model answered a background step in the wrong form

GUID: 83773a62-8a41-43b6-a3e5-d1cbdd804200
Slug: named-tool-contract-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • For a behind-the-scenes step, SMTO asked the model to fill in one specific form. The model sent back a different or broken answer, so SMTO set it aside and did not act on it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and select Check saved model on the Main card, and on the Helper card too if you set one up. SMTO can send some background steps to the Helper model, so either model could have given this answer.
  2. If a check fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs your model service, asking whether it supports choosing a specific tool for the model. This error means the model ignored or mangled the one form SMTO asked for, which depends on that service feature.
  3. If it can't be fixed, pick a model that supports tool calling on that card, select Save, and start a new task. A model that reliably fills in the requested form lets these background steps finish.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, and a new task completes its steps without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages your model service or SMTO. Don't turn off SMTO's safety checks to get past this; the rejected answer was never used, so nothing needs undoing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A forced named-function request (tool_choice naming one result function) returned a response whose structure or function name did not match the requested result function, so validate_named_result rejected it before the result was used.

What this means

  • A bounded named-result call failed envelope or function-name validation; the result cannot stand in for the particular function requested by its caller. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A bounded named-result call failed envelope or function-name validation; the result cannot stand in for the particular function requested by its caller.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect validation_stage and the requested function name; arguments and schema failures have separate categories when validation reaches those stages.

How to fix it

  • Check validation_stage (envelope or tool_name) and expected_tool_name in the error details. Confirm the serving stack honours tool_choice with a named function for this model (for vLLM, a tool-call parser that matches the model), or route this call type to a model that does in Settings › Setup › Model routing. No action from the rejected response was executed.
  • Check the provider’s named tool-choice support before resuming.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A controlled call returns the expected single function and its result validates against the requested schema.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
